solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Old man going round front of African deity’s temple (6)

indicatorNotes.going round: PA travels round the outside of the other letters
indicatorNotes.front of: the front of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: An old man walks around an African god's temple.
annotation.walkthrough: Old man reads as an elderly person, but it is the familiar word for a father. The possessive on deity only joins the wordplay to the definition, temple.
annotation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Buddhist or Hindu temple tower.

entries.clue: Charm of talisman originally supporting a cross (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: the origin of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue, the T sits beneath and holds up the rest

blocks.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

annotation.surface: Someone admires the charm of a talisman hung on a cross.
annotation.walkthrough: Cross looks religious, fitting talisman, but it is the hybrid animal MULE.
annotation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off harm.

entries.clue: Superior? Not in status (11)

blocks.note: OUT (not in) + STANDING (status), read as one word

annotation.surface: A curt note questioning whether a superior really lacks standing.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful split: out = not in, standing = status, which together make the word for superior.
annotation.definitionFit: Outstanding means excellent, clearly superior to others.

entries.clue: Warning over fat, some say, a waxy substance (9)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, AMBER is placed above the next part
indicatorNotes.some say: the next part is spelt as it is spoken

blocks.note: the amber traffic light warns drivers
grease = fat; the spelling here sounds the same when spoken

annotation.surface: A warning about fat mentioning a waxy substance.
annotation.walkthrough: The amber traffic light is the warning before red. GRIS sounds like grease.
annotation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance from sperm whales used in perfume.

entries.clue: Erudite academic with Afghan possibly in Bow (8)

indicatorNotes.in Bow: Bow is in London's Cockney East End, where the H is dropped

blocks.note: an Afghan is a hound; a Cockney drops the H: 'OUND

annotation.surface: A learned academic walks an Afghan hound in East London.
annotation.walkthrough: Afghan wants to be a person but it is the dog breed, and Bow is a Cockney district, so the hound loses its H.
annotation.definitionFit: Profound means showing great knowledge or insight, as erudite does.

entries.clue: Tetchy expression of contempt involving old magistrate endlessly (7)

indicatorNotes.involving: PISH takes the other letters inside it

blocks.note: a reeve was an old local magistrate; REEVE without its ends

annotation.surface: A tetchy person scoffs at an old magistrate.
annotation.walkthrough: Endlessly here removes both ends, not just the last letter: R(EEV)E gives EEV, which goes into P(EEV)ISH.
annotation.definitionFit: Peevish and tetchy both mean irritable.

entries.clue: Old man of wisdom, a Native American of the past (5)

annotation.definition: a Native American of the past
annotation.definitionNote: the Osage nation still exists; the setter pictures its history

blocks.note: a sage is a wise man

annotation.surface: A wise old man described as a Native American of former times.
annotation.walkthrough: Old man reads as one phrase, but O and SAGE are separate.
annotation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

entries.clue: Creature found in oxbow lakes (3)

indicatorNotes.found in: the answer is found inside the next words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the gap between the two words

annotation.surface: A creature spotted living in oxbow lakes.
annotation.walkthrough: An oxbow lake is a curved lake left when a river bend is cut off; its wildlife is a natural setting for a creature.
annotation.definitionFit: Creature is the broadest of category words, standing for any animal, and a bird of prey qualifies.

entries.clue: African abandoned reign after initially breaking hip? (8)

indicatorNotes.abandoned: wild, unrestrained, so the letters of REIGN run loose
indicatorNotes.after: the second part follows the first
indicatorNotes.initially: what comes initially in a word is its opening letter
indicatorNotes.breaking: something that breaks a word splits it open and sits in the gap

annotation.surface: An African ruler gave up the throne after breaking a hip.
annotation.walkthrough: After does two jobs: it places the second part behind the anagram, and its own first letter is what breaks the hip. Abandoned is an adjective meaning wild, not deserted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain nationality: someone from the West African state is an African.

entries.clue: Share regularly billed and apt for citation (8)

annotation.surface: A share is billed at regular intervals and fit to be cited.
annotation.walkthrough: Regularly means every other letter, here the first, third and fifth of billed.
annotation.definitionFit: Something quotable is worth citing.

entries.clue: Declare supporter to be overcome by drink (6)

indicatorNotes.to be overcome by: LEG is swamped by, so held inside, the drink

blocks.note: a leg supports a body or table

annotation.surface: Someone claims a fan was drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: Supporter sounds like a football fan, but it is a limb that holds you up.
annotation.definitionFit: To allege is to declare something without proof.

entries.clue: Worst Irish cause to get moving (6)

blocks.note: to worst someone is to beat them, best them

annotation.surface: The worst Irish cause gets things moving.
annotation.walkthrough: Worst looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning defeat, which is also what best means.
annotation.definitionFit: To bestir someone is to rouse them into action.

entries.clue: Amateurish agent brought back in one immediately following (8)

indicatorNotes.brought back: REP is turned round to PER
indicatorNotes.in: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent

annotation.surface: A clumsy agent is recalled and replaced by the one right behind.
annotation.walkthrough: Agent is a sales rep here, not a spy. One stands in front, and the reversed agent goes into the word for immediately following.
annotation.definitionFit: Inexpert means lacking skill, amateurish.

entries.clue: Eg Raeburn’s characteristic is encapsulated by wine (11)

indicatorNotes.is encapsulated by: TRAIT IS is wrapped inside the wine

annotation.surface: Something typical of the painter Raeburn shows up in his wine.
annotation.walkthrough: Henry Raeburn was an 18th-century Scottish painter. The word is supplies its own letters as well as the verb of the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Raeburn painted the Edinburgh gentry, so he stands for the kind of painter who does likenesses.

entries.clue: English dialect confusing man — Brit or Hun (12)

indicatorNotes.confusing: to confuse is to jumble things together, so the fodder's letters lose their order

annotation.surface: A regional accent baffles a man unsure whether he is British or German.
annotation.walkthrough: Brit or Hun sets up a nationality puzzle, but the answer is a dialect of the far north-east of England.
annotation.definitionFit: Northumbrian is the dialect of Northumberland in north-east England.

entries.clue: Rocky object encountered mounting old English ceremony (9)

indicatorNotes.mounting: in a down clue, climbing up turns OE upside down

annotation.surface: A rocky object turns up at an old English ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: Mounting applies only to OE, which reads upwards as EO.
annotation.definitionFit: A meteorite is a rock from space that lands on Earth.

entries.clue: American Republican publication is able to set up drink (8)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, CAN is raised and so read upwards

annotation.surface: A US Republican magazine is able to organise drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: Set up reads as organise, but in a down answer it means turn upside down, so CAN becomes NAC.
annotation.definitionFit: Drink is the general class; the answer is a particular brandy from Gascony in France.

entries.clue: Anorak Del Boy possibly carries travelling in spa? (12)

indicatorNotes.possibly: Del Boy is one example of a Trotter
indicatorNotes.travelling: the letters of IN SPA move around

blocks.note: Del Boy Trotter, the market trader of the sitcom Only Fools and Horses

annotation.surface: A nerd's jacket that Del Boy might carry on a trip to a spa.
annotation.walkthrough: An anorak is a hooded jacket, but in British slang it is an obsessive hobbyist, the kind who logs train numbers. Del Boy is the wheeler-dealer of a British TV comedy.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang an anorak is a geeky enthusiast, the stereotype being the trainspotter.

entries.clue: Poem about unknown ship on unknown travels (7)

indicatorNotes.about: ODE goes round the next letters
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the last Y

blocks.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

annotation.surface: A poem about a nameless ship on an uncharted voyage.
annotation.walkthrough: Poem hints at Homer's Odyssey, but here ODE is just the wrapper: OD(YSS)E + Y. The definition is travels, a common noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of Odysseus's wanderings gave English a common noun for any long, eventful spell of travels.

entries.clue: Journey’s over in five year period (6)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral five

annotation.surface: A journey ends within a five-year span.
annotation.walkthrough: Over reads as finished, but it is O, sitting inside V + YAGE. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though the answer usually implies a long trip by sea or through space.

entries.clue: Monkey in scruffy state seen around Lincoln? (8)

indicatorNotes.seen around: MANGY is placed around the other name

annotation.surface: A monkey in a scruffy condition spotted near Lincoln.
annotation.walkthrough: Lincoln reads as the English city, but it is the US president, Abe.
annotation.definitionFit: The general term for a specific species: a long-tailed African primate of the forests.

entries.clue: Limited accommodation for rabbit or donkey (5)

indicatorNotes.Limited: cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a burrow, minus its last letter W

annotation.surface: Cramped housing suited to a rabbit or a donkey.
annotation.walkthrough: The rabbit's home is a BURROW; limit it and the W drops.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from Spanish, used in the American Southwest for a small pack donkey.

entries.clue: Certain stars will accept conclusion of this prayer (6)

indicatorNotes.conclusion of: the conclusion of a word is where it ends, its final letter

annotation.surface: Certain stars will receive the closing words of this prayer.
annotation.walkthrough: ORI(S)ON: the stars take in S.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic synonym, from Old French, that survives mainly in poetry and crosswords.

entries.clue: Marksman’s son backtracking about method of authentication (6)

indicatorNotes.backtracking: going back the way it came, so RE PIN is read backwards

blocks.note: a PIN verifies who you are

annotation.surface: A marksman's son retraces his steps over a security check.
annotation.walkthrough: About is not a reversal signal here; it is RE, which goes backwards along with PIN.
annotation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman who shoots from hiding.

entries.clue: Greek character’s afterthought on India (3)

blocks.note: India is I in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A Greek person adds a postscript about India.
annotation.walkthrough: Character is a letter here, not a person. In a down clue, PS on India puts PS above I.
annotation.definitionFit: Character here means a written letter, and this is the 23rd of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Evidence of injury restricting first person with German sword (8)

indicatorNotes.restricting: SCAR confines the other letters inside it

blocks.note: a scar shows an old wound
I is the first person pronoun

annotation.surface: A scar shows where the first man was hurt by a German sword.
annotation.walkthrough: German sword reads as one phrase, but German belongs with with, giving MIT. SC(I MIT)AR.
annotation.definitionFit: The general word for a specific weapon: the curved single-edged blade of the Middle East.

entries.clue: A sidekick bored by this writer’s bitterness (8)

indicatorNotes.bored by: to be bored is to be drilled through, so the other letters pierce it

blocks.note: a crony is a close pal

annotation.surface: A sidekick is bored stiff by the author's resentment.
annotation.walkthrough: Bored reads as weary but means drilled into: A + CR(IM)ONY. This writer is the setter, I, and the 's makes it I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name sharp, resentful ill feeling between people.

entries.clue: Course in French given by elder? (6)

blocks.note: the elder is a tree; the question mark flags an example

annotation.surface: A dish served in French style by an older person.
annotation.walkthrough: Elder looks like an older person, but it is the elder tree.
annotation.definitionFit: A dish served as one stage of a meal; in Britain the starter or middle dish, in America the main one.
